doe-osti-3375565-cybersecurity-workforce:
Argonne National Laboratory report ANL-26/19 lays out a training plan for cyber staff who will guard small modular reactors on local grids. Benjamin Blakely, Jennifer M. Fowler, and Michael Jaynes head the author list. Small reactors will soon plug into local grids beside solar farms and microgrids. That seam, where plant gear meets grid gear, is a fresh attack surface. It comes from the lab's CyDERMS center work.

The team first mapped the rules and the skill gaps. Training on the shelf proved too broad or too narrow for this niche. Their fix is a competency framework with two role tracks and three skill tiers. Twelve learning goals sit at its heart, each tied to a rule set. A hands-on lab runs beside it in software containers. The lab joins a grid model, a reactor transient model, and a SCADA stack, with a library of attack scenes.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-TarsikesJohnGMr: An FBI memorandum dated December 13, 1963, records what Mrs. John G. Tarsikes told the bureau. She identified a young man for investigators, three weeks after President Kennedy was killed in Dallas. Small witness memos like this one fill the early assassination files. Each one shows agents chasing identifications and tips while the case was still raw and unsettled.
